steps.message:
I renamed `userId` to `user_id` in the `GET /users` response (`routes/users.js:6`). It now matches `/orders`. That's the only change, and I haven't committed it.

**This is a breaking change for clients, and it goes against the repo's own rule.** The README says response field names are part of the contract and that changes go through a versioned endpoint. Three known consumers read `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Any of them reading `userId` will get `undefined` once this ships. Old iOS builds stay installed on phones, so updating the clients first won't fully protect you.

Safer options:
- **Return both fields for a while** (`userId` and `user_id`), then drop `userId` once the clients have moved over.
- **Put the rename in a new version** (e.g. `/v2/users`), as the README describes.

If you already know the consumers can handle the change, the edit is ready to commit. Otherwise I can switch it to one of the options above.

arguments.command:
cat > /tmp/patch.py <<'EOF'
import sys
p = sys.argv[1]
s = open(p).read()
old = '''    users.map((u) => ({ user_id: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),'''
new = '''    users.map((u) => ({
      user_id: u.id,
      // Deprecated: kept until all /users consumers read user_id.
      userId: u.id,
      name: u.name,
      email: u.email,
    })),'''
assert old in s
open(p, "w").write(s.replace(old, new))
EOF
python3 -I /tmp/patch.py routes/users.js && git diff && node -e 'const r=require("./routes/users.js");r.listUsers({}, {json:x=>console.log(x[0])})'

steps.message:
I took "go ahead" to mean the non-breaking option. `GET /users` now returns `user_id` and also keeps `userId` with the same value, marked deprecated in a comment (`routes/users.js:6`). Existing clients keep working, and new code can use `user_id`. I ran the handler locally and it returns `{ user_id: 1, userId: 1, name: 'Ada', email: 'ada@example.com' }`.

To finish the rename, remove `userId` once the web app, iOS app and partner export all read `user_id`.

It's not committed yet. If you meant ship the plain rename instead, say so and I'll take out the `userId` line.
